title: Polynomial relative dual and its scalar map over arbitrary bases
statement: Let $R\to A$ be a flat finitely presented homomorphism of arbitrary commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map, def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. Fix a surjection $P=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\twoheadrightarrow A$, where $n\geq0$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Work in ordinary module derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with derived tensor computed on K-flat resolutions [def-pc-module-kflat-complex] and internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] on the one-object ringed site. Put $C=C_{P\to A}(P[0])[n]\in D(A)$, where $C_{P\to A}$ is derived coinduction with precomposition action $(a h)(a')=h(a'a)$ [def-trf-derived-coinduction]. Call $T\in D(A)$ $R$-perfect if it is pseudo-coherent over $A$ [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex] and there exist integers $a_T\leq b_T$ with $H^i(T\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}Q)=0$ for every $R$-module $Q$ and $i\notin[a_T,b_T]$. Then $A[0]$ is perfect over $P$, meaning represented by a bounded complex of finitely generated projective $P$-modules [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex, def-weil-pbc-projective-module]. The complex $C$ is $R$-perfect, and its restriction to $P$ is perfect. The scalar-action morphism $h:A[0]\to R\operatorname{Hom}_A(C,C)$, the transpose of the unit action on $C$, is an isomorphism in $D(A)$. These conclusions include $A=0$ and do not assume Noetherianity.

source.place: Agent arbitrary-base extension of Tag 0BZW, lemma-relative-dualizing-algebraic, proof of (1)(a)--(c) and (2)(a), using polynomial perfectness and finite-presentation descent; not the Noetherian statement verbatim.

proof.text: Write $U:D(A)\to D(P)$ for restriction. The flat finitely presented hypothesis and [lem-sfb-flat-fp-polynomial-pseudocoherent] give pseudo-coherence of $UA[0]$ for this particular surjection, not merely for some presentation. Apply [lem-trf-base-flat-polynomial-tor-bound] to the $P$-module $A$: $\operatorname{Tor}^P_j(A,N)=0$ for $j>n$ and every $P$-module $N$. To express this as derived amplitude, take a projective resolution of $A$ in nonpositive cochain degrees. Its terms are flat by the split-free description [def-weil-pbc-projective-module], so it is K-flat by [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat]. The tensor model [lem-pc-source-kflat-module-tensor-model] and the definition [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules] identify $H^{-j}(A[0]\otimes_P^{\mathbf L}N[0])$ with $\operatorname{Tor}^P_j(A,N)$; positive cochain degrees vanish in that model. Thus $UA[0]$ has Tor amplitude $[-n,0]$.

source.place: Tags 067J (lemma-flat-finite-presentation-perfect), 068X (lemma-perfect-over-polynomial-ring); ordinary Tor and derived tensor definitions

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-finite-tor-perfect] over the commutative ring $P$ to the pseudo-coherent object and finite Tor interval just established. It gives a bounded complex of finitely generated projective $P$-modules representing $UA[0]$. This proves the first assertion, with exactly the meaning of perfect in [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex].

Use the usual symmetric monoidal structure on $D(P)$ supplied by [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal] on the one-object ringed site (with the localization universe chosen equal to the module universe). Put $K=UA[0]$ and $K^\vee=R\operatorname{Hom}_P(K,P[0])$. The perfect-duality lemma [lem-trf-perfect-complex-derived-biduality] gives that $K^\vee$ is perfect and that canonical evaluation $K\to(K^\vee)^\vee$ is an isomorphism. The underlying-object assertion of [lem-trf-derived-coinduction-adjunction] identifies $UC=K^\vee[n]$. Shifting a bounded finite-projective representative simply reindexes its terms, so $UC$ is perfect. In particular it has a bounded-above finite-projective representative; the equivalent characterization of pseudo-coherence in [lem-pc-pseudo-coherent-bounded-finite-free-model] shows that $UC$ is pseudo-coherent over $P$.

source.place: Tags 07VI (lemma-dual-perfect-complex), 0FPT (sites-cohomology, symmetric monoidal structure), and dualizing.tex Tags 0A70--0A71

proof.text: The polynomial algebra $P$ is free as an $R$-module on its monomials, hence $R\to P$ is flat: tensoring an injection with $P$ is the direct sum of copies of that injection. It is finitely presented, with the $n$ variables and no relations, by [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring, def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. Consequently the surjection $P\to A$ satisfies every hypothesis of [lem-sfb-flat-fp-quotient-pseudocoherent] with its intermediate algebra $B=P$. Applying its reverse implication to $C\in D(A)$ and the pseudo-coherence of $UC$ proved in step 3 gives pseudo-coherence of $C$ over $A$.

Choose a bounded finite-projective $P$-complex $E^\bullet$ representing $UC$, and integers $r\le s$ outside which its terms vanish. Every term is a retract of a free $P$-module [def-weil-pbc-projective-module]. Since $P$ is $R$-free on its monomials [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], that free $P$-module is $R$-free; tensoring a split retract of a free module with an injection is a split retract of an injection, hence each $E^j$ is $R$-flat. The restricted complex is K-flat over $R$ by [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat]. Therefore [lem-pc-source-kflat-module-tensor-model] computes $C\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}Q[0]$ by $E^\bullet\otimes_RQ$, which has zero terms, hence zero cohomology, outside $[r,s]$, for every $R$-module $Q$. Together with step 4 this is precisely the $R$-perfectness stipulated in the statement. If $E^\bullet=0$, take $r=s=0$.

source.place: Tag 0BZW, lemma-relative-dualizing-algebraic, proof of (1)(b): the perfect polynomial dual is a bounded base-flat complex

proof.text:
Apply [lem-trf-algebraic-shriek-derived-hom-adjunction] to $P\to A$, $D=C_{P\to A}(P[0])$ and the integer $n$. Its scalar-evaluation compatibility identifies the restriction of the actual scalar-action morphism $h$ under the canonical isomorphism
$$U R\operatorname{Hom}_A(C,C)\ \cong\ R\operatorname{Hom}_P(R\operatorname{Hom}_P(A,P),P)$$
with the canonical bidual map $A[0]\to R\operatorname{Hom}_P(R\operatorname{Hom}_P(A,P),P)$. Specifically, the precomposition action gives $(a\cdot h')(1)=h'(a)$, so this identification concerns the prescribed homothety, not just an abstract isomorphism between its source and target. The bidual map is an isomorphism by [lem-trf-perfect-complex-derived-biduality], applied to the perfect object of step 2 in the symmetric monoidal module derived category [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal]. Restriction $U$ is conservative by [lem-trf-derived-coinduction-adjunction], hence $h$ itself is an isomorphism in $D(A)$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-N6-177af1bba (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: PASS. The six steps follow the proof of Stacks 0BZW (dualizing.tex lemma-relative-dualizing-algebraic, parts (1)(a)-(c) and (2)(a)) for arbitrary bases, with 0E1T substituted for the Noetherian D^b_Coh step. I read 0E1T and 068X in more-algebra.tex. Step 1 uses the 067J pseudo-coherence lemma for the given surjection and the base-flat polynomial Tor bound; the hypothesis that A is flat over R holds. The conversion to Tor amplitude [-n,0] cites projective=summand of free, bounded-above flat => K-flat, the K-flat tensor model and the Tor definition. Step 2: the 0658 criterion gives that A is perfect over P. Step 3: the symmetric monoidal structure on the one-object site meets the hypothesis of the 07VI biduality node. The coinduction node gives UC=K^vee[n]. Pseudo-coherence of UC comes from the 'equivalently f.g. projective' clause in the statement of lem-pc-pseudo-coherent-bounded-finite-free-model. This is a statement-level use, accepted. Step 4: 0E1T applies with B=P (P is free on monomials, so flat and finitely presented; P->A is surjective). Step 5: bounded P-projective terms are R-flat, so the complex is K-flat over R and the amplitude is [r,s]. Step 6: the mixed RHom adjunction maps the actual scalar map h to the canonical bidual map. That map is an iso by biduality, and U is conservative, so h is an iso. Edge cases A=0, R=0, n=0 and A=P all go through. Duplicates: the 0BZW and perfect/pseudo-coherent searches found only Noetherian finite-type versions (lem-trf-algebraic-shriek-relative-perfect, lem-trf-flat-polynomial-quotient-perfect) and siblings with different conclusions. None restates the item. There is no cycle and no SGA citation. Batch 5: the four newly cited trf nodes are general commutative/homological algebra. They are the base-flat polynomial Tor bound, 07VI perfect biduality, 0A70/0A71 coinduction, and the mixed RHom adjunction. Their closures contain no trace-formula or Poincare-duality statement or step and no nt-assume leaf, so they lie outside the assumptions and are accepted. The tool_uses in split_report are generic tools and are accepted. No new nodes and no changes.
